questions.question: Draw the graphs of the following sets of lines. In each case, reflect on the role of 'a' and 'b'. **(i)** $y = 4x$, $y = 2x$, $y = x$ **(ii)** $y = -6x$, $y = -3x$, $y = -x$ **(iii)** $y = 5x$, $y = -5x$ **(iv)** $y = 3x - 1$, $y = 3x$, $y = 3x + 1$ **(v)** $y = -2x - 3$, $y = -2x$, $y = 2x + 3$

solution.content: **Recall the general form:** Every line of the form $y = ax + b$ is a straight line. Here $a$ is the **slope** and $b$ is the **y-intercept** (where the line cuts the y-axis).

**(i) $y = 4x$, $y = 2x$, $y = x$:** All three lines have $b = 0$, so they all pass through the origin $(0, 0)$. As $a$ increases (1, 2, 4), the lines become steeper. All rise left to right — they represent **linear growth**.

**(ii) $y = -6x$, $y = -3x$, $y = -x$:** Again $b = 0$, so all three pass through the origin. Now $a < 0$, so the lines **fall** from left to right — they represent **linear decay**. As $|a|$ increases (1, 3, 6), the lines become steeper.

**(iii) $y = 5x$, $y = -5x$:** Both pass through the origin. $y = 5x$ rises (positive slope) while $y = -5x$ falls (negative slope). They are **mirror images** of each other across the x-axis and have the same steepness since $|a| = 5$ for both.

**(iv) $y = 3x - 1$, $y = 3x$, $y = 3x + 1$:** Here $a = 3$ is fixed and $b$ varies ($-1$, $0$, $1$). All three lines have the **same slope**, so they are **parallel** to each other. They are shifted vertically: $y = 3x - 1$ cuts the y-axis at $(0, -1)$, $y = 3x$ at $(0, 0)$, and $y = 3x + 1$ at $(0, 1)$.

**(v) $y = -2x - 3$, $y = -2x$, $y = 2x + 3$:** The lines $y = -2x - 3$ and $y = -2x$ have the same slope $-2$, so they are **parallel**; $y = -2x - 3$ is $y = -2x$ shifted down by 3 units. The line $y = 2x + 3$ has slope $+2$ (rising) and cuts the y-axis at $(0, 3)$.

**Summary of the roles of $a$ and $b$:** (1) $a$ is the slope: if $a > 0$ the line rises (linear growth); if $a < 0$ the line falls (linear decay); larger $|a|$ means steeper. (2) $b$ is the y-intercept: the line cuts the y-axis at $(0, b)$. (3) Lines with the same $a$ but different $b$ are parallel.

questions.answer: (i) All pass through origin, steeper as a grows. (ii) All pass through origin, falling; steeper as |a| grows. (iii) y=5x rises, y=−5x falls; mirror images. (iv) Parallel lines (same slope 3), shifted by b. (v) y=−2x−3 and y=−2x are parallel; y=2x+3 rises. a = slope, b = y-intercept.

formulaBox.title: Roles of a and b in y = ax + b
formulaBox.content: $$a = \text{slope (steepness and direction)}, \qquad b = \text{y-intercept (point } (0,b) \text{ on the y-axis)}$$

questions.notes:
**Key Result:** Lines with equal slopes are parallel. Lines with the same y-intercept meet at that point on the y-axis.

**Graphing Tip:** To draw $y = ax + b$, find two points — the y-intercept $(0, b)$ and one more point by choosing a convenient $x$ — then join them with a straight edge and extend.
